newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian spot natgas off on warm western weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas off on warm western weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices softened by a few cents on Wednesday as western Canadian temperatures remained warm and players grew less anxious over refilling depleted storage volumes, traders said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was talked at C$1.65 per gigajoule, down from C$1.67 on Tuesday and C$1.86 last week.
June and summer AECO prices were quoted at C$1.64/1.65 per GJ, down about a cent from Tuesday.
"It's the weather and storage is getting in there a bit better now," a Calgary-based trader said.
Environment Canada said southern Alberta temperatures were forecast to hit highs of 26 Celsius (79 Fahrenheit) on Thursday and Friday, but cool to 16 Celsius (61 Fahreneit) on the weekend.
At the borders, Niagara and other points in the TransCanada PipeLines eastern Canadian zone were discussed at US$2.40/US$2.42 per million British thermal units, up about five cents from Tuesday.
One trader of eastern Canadian gas said he expected Niagara and Dawn in southern Ontario to remain strong over the next few days.
"I think cash will continue to follow the NYMEX, and the NYMEX is really strong," he said.
June NYMEX gas futures closed Wednesday's session up US$0.087 to US$2.276 per mmBtu.
